name: Brian John Adams
notable_stories: Was first seen by Robin Smiley, who called him 'little Brie.'
As a toddler, he ate the hair off an Ernie finger puppet during a family move to San Diego
He later charged a nickel for neighborhood kids to see his new baby brother, Brendan

As a high school junior Brian went to Europe to play soccer with coach Cliff McCrath (ODP and Seattle Pacific University), and carried a crystal vase from Czechoslovakia home for his mother, packed in his socks and underwear.
In high school Brian made lifelong friends John Nordstrom, Mark McGee and David Schmaltz.

Getting the mower out, Brian put his mother's car in neutral and it rolled down the steep driveway, across the road and into the blackberries, which stopped it; he then dented it with an axe trying to chop the brambles away.

As a toddler dressed all in blue, Brian was taken for a girl by a stranger at the Mount Vernon mall and told her, 'You are a real winner, lady,' repeating what his mother had just said to a driver who stole her parking spot.
In high school Brian travelled to four countries to play soccer for coach Cliff McCrath, and brought his mother back a crystal vase stuffed with his underwear and socks so it would not break.
milestones: Bachelor of Science in Psychology, University of Washington, Seattle
Salem, OR — while Michelle attended law school
Master's degree and PhD in Psychology, University of Tennessee, Knoxville
Father of Ethan, Gabrielle, Lauren, and Gavin
Religion: Brian was baptized by the parish priest of the Navy base parish in Meridian, Mississippi. (1972)

Religion: Brian made his First Communion on the day Mount St. Helens erupted (Sunday, 18 May 1980), with Granny and Pops, Nana and Papa, and Aunt Rosemary and Uncle Ralph attending; he was also baptized, made his first confession and was confirmed.

After San Diego the family settled in a house on Whidbey Island, where John was soon deployed; there little Brian picked out two goldfish, named them Ernie and Bert, and was found lifting them out of the bowl onto the kitchen counter. (about 1973-1975)
education: Went to preschool in Oak Harbor as a toddler.
Went to school in Gilroy, where his mother volunteered in his classroom (first grade) in the mornings.
Went to Catholic school in Kelso and graduated from high school while the family lived there.
Brian entered St. Rose School in second grade when the family moved to Kelso, then went to Coweeman Junior High and Kelso High School, where he was a sophomore in 1988 and later graduated.
career: Brian works as a psychologist, and his father calls his empathy for people with mental-health struggles his model of compassion.
sources: John Howard Adams, "John Howard Adams - A Memoir" (privately printed)
Barbara McKeldin Adams, "Barbara McKeldin Adams - A Memoir" (privately printed)
notes: Barbara says the meaning of Brian was 'high, noble, dark one, warrior.'
